title: Building efficient hybrid context query for LLM grounding: Simrat Hanspal

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary focus is building hybrid RAG queries combining semantic vector search with structured relational filters for LLM grounding. The e-commerce search use case maps to search and knowledge systems, while Hasura serves as the developer platform enabling unified GraphQL data APIs. The talk covers both building RAG query pipelines in development and securing them with role-based permissions for production deployment. The talk requires prior familiarity with RAG, vector databases, GraphQL APIs, and permission models. Recorded conference talk with live Streamlit demonstrations of semantic, structured, and hybrid queries plus a security vulnerability demo. summary: Simrat Hanspal introduces the challenge of building efficient hybrid context queries for RAG applications, using e-commerce product search as the primary use case. Present-day product search is keyword-based and cannot fully capture user intent. Product search queries can be contextual (descriptive, semantic similarity via vector DB), structured (relational fields like price and category in Postgres), or hybrid (combining both elements). LLMs are frozen in time and cannot solve tasks on unseen data without context, motivating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). A critical concern is that GenAI applications must not leak sensitive data even when prompted, a primary enterprise concern. The speaker explains a paradigm shift: traditional data-driven applications treat data as constant with evolving software, whereas RAG applications require data to adapt dynamically to natural language queries with no structural limitations, expanding the attack surface. Hasura addresses this by enabling unified, dynamic, secure GraphQL data APIs over multiple data sources. The demo connects vector DB (pgvector) and relational tables via Hasura, using event triggers for auto-vectorization. A Streamlit app calls OpenAI to generate GraphQL queries from natural language. Three query types are demonstrated: pure semantic ("essential oils for relaxation"), structured ("products less than $500"), and hybrid ("essential oil diffusers in price range $500-$1000"). A security vulnerability is then shown where a malicious prompt generates an insert mutation that succeeds. The fix involves creating a restricted role ("product_search_b") with only select/search permissions, which blocks the unauthorized insert. The talk concludes that Hasura enables building hybrid query context for sophisticated, secure RAG applications.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: Product search queries span semantic (vector similarity), structured (relational filters), and hybrid (both combined) types, each requiring different data retrieval strategies.
LLMs are frozen in time and need RAG to access unseen data, making context retrieval essential for grounded, accurate answers.
GenAI introduces a paradigm shift where data must dynamically adapt to natural language queries, removing structural limitations and expanding security attack surfaces.
Hasura provides a unified, dynamic, secure GraphQL API across multiple data sources (relational and vector DBs), avoiding the need for separate data APIs per query type.
Hasura event triggers can auto-vectorize records into a vector DB as new data is inserted into relational tables.
A Streamlit app with OpenAI integration can generate GraphQL queries from natural language input, which are then executed on Hasura for context retrieval.
Without proper role-based permissions, malicious prompts can generate and execute unauthorized mutations (e.g., inserting fake products), demonstrating a real security risk in RAG applications.
Defining a restricted Hasura role with only select/search permissions effectively blocks unauthorized mutation operations like inserts.
Role-based access control in the data API layer is critical for production-ready RAG pipelines that handle sensitive enterprise data.
Hasura enables building hybrid query context for sophisticated RAG applications like product search with built-in security.

sections.title: Introduction and Problem Statement
sections.summary: Simrat Hanspal introduces hybrid RAG queries using e-commerce product search. Current keyword-based search fails to capture full intent. Product search can be contextual (descriptive), structured (field-based), or both. LLMs are frozen in time and need RAG to access unseen data, generating more accurate grounded answers.

sections.title: Security Concerns and Paradigm Shift
sections.summary: GenAI applications must not leak sensitive data even if prompted. A paradigm shift is occurring: traditional data-driven apps treat data as constant with evolving software, while RAG apps require data to dynamically adapt to natural language queries with no structural limitations, expanding the attack surface. Hasura provides unified, dynamic, secure GraphQL data APIs.

sections.title: Demo Setup and Data Sources
sections.summary: The demo connects multiple data sources via Hasura's GraphQL API. For simplicity, only pgvector is used, containing vectors plus price and category structured fields. Hasura event triggers auto-vectorize new records inserted into the Postgres table into the vector DB. A Streamlit app connects to Hasura endpoint and OpenAI for chat completion.

sections.title: Query Demos: Semantic, Structured, and Hybrid
sections.summary: Three query types are demonstrated: pure semantic ('essential oils for relaxation' via vector similarity), structured ('products less than $500' via price filter), and hybrid ('essential oil diffusers in price range $500-$1,000' combining semantic and structured filters). Each generates a GraphQL query executed on Hasura, returning correct results.

sections.title: Security Vulnerability and Role-Based Fix
sections.summary: A malicious prompt generates an insert mutation that successfully inserts a fake product (ID 7,001) into the database. To fix this, a new restricted role 'product_search_b' is created with only select/search permissions. Retesting the same malicious insert (ID 7,002) correctly returns a permission error. The talk concludes with a recap of using Hasura for secure hybrid query context in sophisticated RAG applications.

demonstrations: Streamlit app connecting to Hasura endpoint with admin secret and OpenAI API key for chat completion
Semantic search query: 'show me essential oils for relaxation' generating a GraphQL query with vector similarity search
Structured search query: 'show me all products less than price $500' generating GraphQL with price filter
Hybrid search query: 'looking for essential oil diffusers in the price range of $500 to $1,000' combining semantic and structured filters
Security vulnerability demo: malicious prompt requesting insertion of a product with ID 7,001 that succeeded via generated insert mutation
Security fix: creating a new role 'product_search_b' with only search/select permissions, then retesting the malicious insert (ID 7,002) which was correctly blocked
Hasura console showing data tab with pgvector tables containing vectors, price, and category fields
Hasura console API tab for executing and testing GraphQL queries
limitations: Demo used only vector DB (pgvector) for simplicity rather than showcasing multiple data sources simultaneously
Security role configuration was kept very simple with no additional checks and all columns accessible
Only happy flows and one malicious flow were demonstrated; broader unhappy flows not covered
Demo did not show the full multi-source hybrid query (relational + vector) intersection operation mentioned in the problem statement
quantitativeClaims: 12+ years of prior experience as Applied Data Scientist (from speaker bio in description)
Four different data sources can be connected with Hasura (mentioned but only pgvector used in demo for simplicity)
Demo used price ranges: less than $500 and between $500-$1,000
